findings.issue: Input 10000000000000001 and corresponding expected values were outside the JavaScript safe integer domain and rounded during JSON.parse.
findings.resolution: Author replaced them with 1000000000001 and exact represented expected values before the reviewed baseline run.

findings.issue: Exact delete marker was not distinguished from numeric 1 by Python equality; nested list true-versus-1 replacement also needed a regression case.
findings.resolution: Author added numeric-delete ValueError and nested list type-change expected-output checks and exact marker validation.

findings.issue: A top-level delete marker had no key to target, leaving whole-layer behavior ambiguous.
findings.resolution: R02 now restricts directives to nested patch values and root-delete asserts ValueError.

findings.issue: Letters or digits was narrower than the implemented Unicode alphanumeric token class, which includes non-ASCII numeric characters such as a fraction.
findings.resolution: R01 now explicitly specifies Unicode alphanumeric characters and an acceptance case exercises a non-ASCII numeric token.

findings.issue: Sorted object keys plus recursive traversal do not imply global lexical ordering of dotted paths when sibling keys contain punctuation. Existing expected cases were correct but did not cover this boundary.
findings.resolution: A punctuation-prefix path-order case now requires [a!,a.x]; the independent expected-value model already sorted final paths and agrees. Final fixture and baseline receipt are rebound.
